content.title: Kate Hudson corrected a red-carpet reporter at the Oscars after they mistakenly said she previously won an award
content.text: Kate Hudson attended the 2023 Oscars on March 12. Mike Coppola/Getty Images Mar 13, 2023, 3:52 PM UTC Kate Hudson corrected a red-carpet reporter at the 2023 Oscars who mistakenly believed she previously won an award. The interaction happened on Sunday at the Dolby Theatre in Los Angeles, California, before the annual awards ceremony. Hudson wore a sparkling gown designed by Rodarte when she stopped for a brief interview with an ABC reporter. "Kate, you know what it's like to win an Oscar," the reporter said. Kate paused before responding: "I have never won an Oscar, but I've been nominated." She added: "I'm sure it's amazing." Viewers called out the moment on Twitter, with one user calling the moment "cringey." "ABC is so cringey to watch work the red carpet…this moderator just told Kate Hudson congrats on her Oscar…AND SHES NEVER WON AN OSCAR," they wrote. Another wrote: "Most awkward moment of the night so far: A presenter mistaking that Kate Hudson has an Oscar. "I've never won an Oscar." Hudson snagged a best supporting actress nod for her role in the 2001 film "Almost Famous," but Marcia Gay Harden clinched the award for the movie "Pollock." Hudson's most recent film, "Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery," received a nomination for best adapted screenplay at this year's Oscars but lost to Sarah Polley's "Women Talking." Kate Hudson (left) in "Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery." Netflix Other celebrities, including model Ashley Graham and actor Hugh Grant, went viral for their red-carpet moments last night. Twitter users branded Graham's interview with Grant as awkward. During the interview, Graham asked Grant what he was wearing. "Just my suit," Grant replied. Graham later asked about his cameo in "Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery," but got a short response. "Well, I'm barely in it. I'm in it for about three seconds," Grant said.
